changes: Restore the floating terminal status row to its original horizontal/vertical padding; remove build 22's internal 48-point footer reservation. Keep terminal grid/PTY reflow on docking.

Vend one UIInputView wrapper containing the original SwiftTerm row; reserve 48 trailing points for the system resize corner. Retain original key targets/layout and bridge sticky Ctrl through the public TerminalView modifier/reset notification API.

Use the full UIKit keyboard end rectangle, including the accessory, for one workspace inset. Disable separate SwiftUI keyboard avoidance so alternate-keyboard reloads cannot obscure the status row. Undocked keyboards do not shrink the whole workspace.
Size the alternate input view from the current app window instead of UIScreen bounds.
Add actual accessory-button expand/collapse checks and focused window/focus regressions only.
Keep saved user frames independent of temporary viewport constraints; constrain displayed copies only and retain the same Metal canvas across background/resume and frame revisions.
Position new windows relative to existing displayed, constrained origins while retaining their preferred saved frames.

Measure the actual system-app viewport at the scene root and host the terminal scroll view in a plain UIKit viewport; system window resizing relayouts the same terminal without requiring a model change or internal docking.

Send the current live grid on deferred size notifications so stale snapshots cannot overwrite a completed app-window resize. Verify actual Linux stty size after four native app-container size transitions.
Rebind final buttons after UIKit finishes assigning the original row bounds; handle real upstream button rebuilds without losing keyboard-toggle accessibility identity or sticky Ctrl forwarding.

diagnosis.window_geometry: Both the saved workspace frames and the local SwiftUI state were destructively constrained by transient viewport changes. Keep preferred frames and constrain displayed copies; only user gestures save altered geometry. Rust pause and Metal foreground recovery do not explicitly delete top-level surfaces.
diagnosis.keyboard: Accessory-controller variants passed standalone tests but left an empty row in the actual UIKit attachment path. The final version vends exactly one wrapper as inputAccessoryView and does not override inputAccessoryViewController. It retains original key behavior and bridges the upstream public Ctrl modifier/reset API explicitly. The plain wrapper renders correctly and leaves the measured trailing gap; UIKit then invokes the child bounds observer and rebuilds the buttons after the parent binding pass. Coalesced post-layout rebinding retains IDs and Ctrl targets on the actual displayed controls.
diagnosis.scope: No GPU, guest, native library or File Provider implementation changes in this follow-up.
